items.s: The job was ____: she did the same small task in the same order every day.
The news was ____, so nobody had prepared for it.
Too many deadlines can make a job very ____ and leave people feeling worried.
Many retired people want to do something ____, like helping others, so their days feel important.
Children learn fast because their ____ makes them ask questions all the time.

match.d: feel pleased about something that will happen
unhappy because you have nobody around you
keep your mind quick and clear
take action to handle a problem or situation

items.s: A study from Germany, ____ in 2026, asked an interesting question.
The change ____ some women wait longer before retiring early.
Retirement ____ wonderful to many people.
Spending longer in retirement ____ to lower scores on some tasks.
This ____ the researchers to compare people who left work at different times.

tfn.s: The researchers studied one particular group of women in Germany.
tfn.why: The text says: "The study looked at a particular group of German women and the effects of a specific change in the law."

tfn.s: Some health measures, such as sleep problems, improved in retirement.
tfn.why: The text says: "In fact, some health measures, including sleep problems and depression, improved."

tfn.s: Most German women now retire before the age of sixty.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say at what age most German women now retire.

tfn.s: The researchers found that retirement causes dementia.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "This is not the same as saying that retirement causes dementia."

tfn.s: All kinds of knowledge showed the same decline in retirement.
tfn.why: The text says: "other kinds of knowledge did not show the same decline."

pre.d: people you work with
people who study something to find new facts
facts that show something is true
a slow fall to a lower level
working to help other people without being paid
making you very, very tired
difficult things that test you
stop being there

focus.note: Some adjectives and nouns need one fixed preposition. Learn the pair as one chunk, for example worried about.

items.s: Retirement can be a big change for people who are used ____ a busy job.
Many people are proud ____ the work they did.
How happy people feel may depend ____ their plans.
There was a rise ____ the number of retired people who volunteer.
Some people worry ____ having too much free time after they stop working.
The council published its plan ____ a detailed map of the new bus routes.
Starting a job in a new industry, she found many of the tools ____ because she had never used them before.
He never touched the guitar again, and the instrument sat ____ in the attic for years.
Her ____ experience, built up over forty years in the job, made her the natural choice to lead the team.
If safety checks are ignored, accidents will ____ happen sooner or later.
Workers who ____ easily when tools change usually cope better with new systems.

match.d: stay at the same level as something that is changing quickly
say or do more than is reasonable
interesting enough to make you think

items.s: By the time she turned sixty, she ____ to leave her job.
The early retirement age for certain women ____ by the reform.
If he had known about the study, he ____ it.
Since she retired, she ____ up painting and joined a choir.
At nine o'clock last Friday, she ____ her farewell speech.

tfn.s: Accumulated knowledge declined in the same way as flexible thinking.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "accumulated knowledge was not affected in the same way."

tfn.s: Similar research has been carried out on German men.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not mention any research on German men.

tfn.s: The researchers could compare women whose time in retirement differed because of the reform.
tfn.why: The reform "created an opportunity to study the effects of spending different lengths of time in retirement."

tfn.s: According to the text, staying in work is always the healthier choice.
tfn.why: The text says there is "no reason to assume that staying employed is automatically the healthiest choice."

tfn.s: Some health indicators got better with extra time in retirement.
tfn.why: The text says depression, sleep problems and high blood pressure "actually improved".

pre.d: an official change to a law or system
a plan of action that a government or organisation agrees
decisions about which illness a person has
signs that show what something is like
needing a lot of time, effort or skill
real, not false
the reason for doing something
keep something at the same level

focus.note: A verb, adjective or noun often takes one fixed preposition. Check which one follows before you choose, because the same idea can need a different word in your own language.

items.s: Many people benefit ____ having a clear routine after leaving work.
Good planning contributes ____ a smoother change from work to retirement.
Some retirees rely ____ a small pension and part-time work.
Retired people are welcome to take part ____ the club's weekly events.
He is fond ____ his old colleagues and still sees them every week.
Rival firms quickly ____ the loophole in the regulations before it was closed.
To reach a fair verdict, the panel needed ____ evidence rather than personal impressions.
Several factors played a role, but ____, the funding never arrived.
Given proper support, many small businesses ____ and expand into new markets.
The engineers solved the problem with a ____ approach that nobody had tried before.
A one-year course is not ____ to a full degree, although it may earn you credit.

match.d: far too general to be accurate
so hard that it wears you down
giving you a welcome new sense of freedom

items.s: Strict ____ rules meant that only a few applicants qualified.
Much of the delay was caused by ____ errors, not by any lack of funding.
Early signs for the proposed merger were distinctly ____.
Some people struggle to cope with a completely ____ day.
Her experience made her ____ to the team.

tfn.s: The study's design gives stronger evidence about retirement than comparing people who chose when to stop.
tfn.why: The text says such a design "offers stronger evidence" than simply comparing people who stopped at different ages.

tfn.s: The findings could be applied with confidence to men who retire early.
tfn.why: The text says the effects "cannot automatically be applied to men, younger retirees or workers in other countries."

tfn.s: The authors recommend raising the retirement age across Europe.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say that the authors recommend raising the retirement age anywhere.

tfn.s: The study found weaker scores on some tests alongside improvements in some health indicators.
tfn.why: The text reports weaker fluid intelligence and also better hypertension, depression and sleep indicators.

tfn.s: The study suggests that knowledge built up over a lifetime is the first thing to weaken in retirement.
tfn.why: The text says crystallised intelligence "appeared less affected" than fluid intelligence.

pre.d: a group of people born or starting at the same time
make something harder to understand or deal with
completely
people who have stopped working because of their age
keep something from being lost or changed
making or creating something again
connected with thinking and understanding
in a way that lasts a long time or keeps coming back

focus.note: Some adjectives are followed by one fixed preposition, and the pair often sounds formal or negative. Learn the whole chunk, not just the adjective.

items.s: Telling experienced workers to leave at fifty-five would be tantamount ____ wasting their skills.
The move into retirement can be fraught ____ difficulty for people who have no plans.
Whether the scheme succeeds is contingent ____ how many people take part.
Retirees who feel bereft ____ purpose may find that volunteering helps.
Many long-established firms are steeped ____ tradition, which can make change slow.

speak.title: Role-play: a friend who wants to retire early
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.role: the colleague who wants to retire early
a.text: You'll be sixty next year and you'd like to stop working. Tell your friend your plans and why you want to go. Answer their questions and decide whether to change your mind.

b.role: the friend who is not sure
b.text: Your colleague wants to retire early. You're worried they'll miss work and have too little to do. Ask questions and suggest ideas, but listen to their reasons.

phrases: I've been thinking about retiring early.
What would you do with all that free time?
That's a fair point, but I'd rather stop now.
I'd like to learn a language and join a choir.
Why don't you work part-time first?
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did the friend change their mind, and what was the best idea?
